messages:
Maya: AspenEdge just opened a high-priority ticket — p99 on /v1/embeddings jumped from ~900ms to ~5s starting 03:00 UTC, intermittent 504s. Customer says impact on search relevance. They included trace id trc-8a2f9c. Can SRE take a look?
Liam: Escalated and shared customer context + SLA note. They're on Dedicated but not pinned; sharing a medium GPU pool. Asked for immediate mitigation options.
Nate: On it. Looking at tenant-level metrics — I see sustained token throughput spikes from tenant_id=aspenedge-prod coincident with p99 tail. Node g-17 has elevated GPU memory churn and long RPC queue times. Suspect noisy neighbor workload causing KV cache churn.
Sophia: Runtime side shows frequent KV cache evictions and fluctuating attention-kernel latencies. Also GC-ish pauses on the process around the same timestamps. Packet of requests with huge declared batch sizes but tiny payloads — seems like a client-side batching bug causing oversized batch windows.
Maya: Customer says they can't patch their client instantly. They want temporary relief (allowlist, reservation, or throttling) while they fix their ingest.
Nate: Immediate mitigation plan: (A) create a soft reservation for aspenedge to give baseline capacity, (B) apply a per-tenant throttle to smooth bursts, (C) enable a circuit-breaker fallback to a smaller/quantized model for requests that hit the latency threshold. I can run A+B now. Will coordinate with Runtime for C.
Sophia: For the fallback, we can set route-level `fallback_on_timeout` to true and point to `rwd-small-quant`. Example config snippet:```json
{"route":"/v1/embeddings","primary_model":"rwd-embed-v2","fallback_model":"rwd-embed-v1-quant","timeout_ms":1500,"max_concurrency":8}```That should keep p95 low while preserving correctness for most requests.
Nate: Commands I'm about to run (dry-run logged):
```
# create soft reservation (non-destructive)
redwoodctl reservation create --tenant aspenedge-prod --pool medium-gpu --gpu-count 1 --mode soft --duration 48h
# set per-tenant throttle
redwoodctl throttle set --tenant aspenedge-prod --qps 12 --burst 30
```
Maya: Applied reservation + throttle. Customer reports initial improvement: p95 went from ~1.6s to ~230ms. p99 improved but still has occasional 4-5s spikes.
Sophia: We rolled the fallback route for the embedding path for aspensedge-prod. Logs show ~12% of requests hit fallback during the first 10 minutes (those were timing out on primary). Fallback latency p95 ~180ms, p99 ~700ms.
Nate: Added an isolation job to pin aspensedge to a short-lived dedicated slice tonight for 6 hours to observe. If noisy pattern continues, we'll recommend a reserved capacity plan. Also setting an alert: tenant p99 > 1s for 5m.
Anya: Filing a product action item to add an automatic soft-reservation suggestion when tenant p99 delta > x and noisy neighbor heuristics trigger. RFC created: RFC-2456.
telemetry-bot: [alert] tenant=aspensedge-prod p99_latency=4.8s window=03:03:21-03:08:21 — mitigation applied: soft_reservation + throttle + fallback — resolved after 03:12:04.
Maya: Customer confirmed improved UX, will try rolling client fix tomorrow. Asked for follow-up report and guidance on how to avoid this pattern (small payloads + large declared batch windows). I'll close after 48h monitor if stable. :white_check_mark:
